title: Event bus requirements and scope
idea: Scoping a pub-sub event bus means fixing how publishers reach subscribers through topics, which delivery guarantee you promise, and what v1 leaves out.
points: Publishers send events to a named topic and never know who listens.
Every subscriber of a topic receives each event, independently of the others.
Delivery is at-least-once: a failed handler is retried, then parked as a dead letter.
Events with the same key reach each subscriber in publish order.

hero.caption: In v1, retries stop losses while the process runs; subscribers skip repeated event ids. Surviving a restart needs a durable store.

code.title: Scope as an enum
code.caption: Each requirement carries its kind, so the v1 cut is data you can print and check against interview asks.

walk.text: Group every requirement by kind in an EnumMap, which keeps enum order.
Print each group with its size, then its requirements.
Answer three interview asks: is this in v1 or not?
Five functional needs: topics, publish, subscribe, unsubscribe, dead letters.
Four qualities: at-least-once, per-key order, isolation, thread safety.
Durability, clustering and exactly-once are named as out on purpose.

pitfalls: Ask whether events must survive a restart; in-memory and durable buses differ greatly.
Promise order per key, not across the whole topic; global order kills parallelism.
Never promise exactly-once; offer at-least-once with idempotent subscribers instead.

quiz.q: An interviewer asks for exactly-once delivery in v1. Best scoping answer?
options: Promise it, because retries make delivery exact
Switch to at-most-once so nothing repeats
At-least-once, with subscribers that skip repeated event ids
Remove retries so duplicates cannot happen
quiz.why: Retries are what stop losses, and retries can repeat a delivery. Remembering handled event ids makes repeats harmless, which gives the effect of exactly-once.

takeaway: Fix topics, the delivery guarantee and per-key order before drawing classes.
